entities.summary:
Lionsgate Films, founded in Vancouver in 1997 and now headquartered in Santa Monica, is the largest independent film studio in Hollywood — producing Saw (2004), Hostel (2005), Crash (2004 Best Picture), The Hunger Games franchise ($2.95 billion worldwide), the Twilight franchise ($3.3 billion), and John Wick franchise, while also distributing Michael Moore's Fahrenheit 9/11 (the highest-grossing documentary in US history). Lionsgate's success demonstrated that an independent studio could compete with the six major studios by identifying genre niches (horror, action, young adult) and executing them efficiently.

Lionsgate was founded by Frank Giustra with Jon Feltheimer as CEO, growing rapidly through acquisitions including Artisan Entertainment (2003, gaining American History X, Pi, and The Blair Witch Project's library), Trimark Pictures, and Summit Entertainment (2012, gaining Twilight). The studio's horror strategy — low-budget, high-return R-rated films — was perfected with Saw ($103 million worldwide on $1.2 million budget) and continued with 7 sequels grossing $980 million total.

The Hunger Games ($2.95 billion worldwide) and Twilight ($3.3 billion) demonstrated Lionsgate's ability to acquire and execute young adult (YA) franchise properties before the major studios recognized the genre's potential. Lionsgate's STARZ acquisition (2016, $4.4 billion) and STARZ streaming platform (now 41+ million subscribers) transformed it from pure film studio to diversified media company. The John Wick franchise ($1+ billion) demonstrated Lionsgate's ability to launch original franchises.
